Job Description: Mechanical Engineer

A Mechanical Engineer at United Science develops manufacturing processes by studying product requirements;

researching, designing, modifying, and testing specifications and manufacturing methods and equipment.

Duties and Responsibilities of Mechanical Engineer

• Work on product development or sustaining projects, which involve design, replacement or redesign for

obsolete components, product improvement features, cost reduction, manufacturing support, and field

complaints.

• Prepare assembly or product layout and detailed drawings, and participate in the manufacture or building of

prototype product or system.

• Provide tolerances studies, apply GD&T, conduct stress-analysis studies, develop reliability testing

procedures, and generates appropriate design verification reports.

• Design testing methods to analyze product capabilities and troubleshoot any mechanical or structural flaws.

Perform analysis tests to track results and make improvements.

• Recommend design changes, cost reductions, warranty improvements, and manufacturing issues.

• Work with marketing and vendors, providing product specifications for their use.

• Ensure that design implementation, test, and maintenance methods/processes are developed and executed in

a manner that supports company quality standards.

• Write product specifications, document test results, prepare product operating instructions and review

technical literature.

• Participate in test runs or field installations.

• Participate in scheduled department meetings to report progress of overall project or portion of project, and

prepare and give design presentations, and mentor junior engineers and technicians.

Mechanical Engineer Skills and Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology

• Strong ability with computer-aided design systems and experience with mathematical computing and analysis

tools knowledge (SolidWorks, AutoCad, PDM).

• Superior computer skills; well-versed in Microsoft Office Suite (particularly strong with Excel);

• Able to create 2-D or 3-D designs to run simulations, analyze, and tests

JOB TITLE: Mechanical Designer

EFFECTIVE DATE: 11/04/2021

DEPARTMENT: Engineering

SUMMARY OF FUNCTIONS:

The Mechanical Designer uses computer aided design and development (CADD) techniques to prepare

drawings, diagrams, illustrations and schematics for product documentation/literature and all types of

publications according to company and regulatory specifications and standards.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Proficiently utilizing CAD software for drafting and illustrating including three-dimensional

perspectives of documentation to satisfy documentation requirements for Engineering,

Manufacturing, Marketing and Customer Service.

• Renders new product concept illustrations from free-hand sketches or marketing or engineering

input. Makes suggestions to product committee on various design requirements and

recommends possible solutions or alternate constructions. Prepares evaluations of strength of

materials, tolerances and stresses, weights and cubed dimensions.

• Prepares new or improved product and component documents for engineering and

manufacturing including layouts, blueprints, assembly and detail drawings. This can also include

development of drawings for special tools, fixtures, process and test equipment.

• Creates product or component illustrations including block diagrams, schematics, isometric

illustrations, orthographic illustrations and three-dimensional perspective illustrations for use in

marketing literature, manuals and sales video presentations.

• Creates exploded-view drawings for operation, service and assembly manuals from product and

component detail drawings and bill of materials in accordance with operating/set-up

instructions or assembly/disassembly breakdowns.

• Provides other drafting and illustrating services as needed by engineering, production, customer

service or as requested by the management.

ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS:

Reports directly to the CEO. Coordinates activities with Engineers, Designers, Marketing,

Production, and Customer Service Departments.

QUALIFICATIONS:

A college degree is preferred with a major in graphics design preferred. Good communication skills and

the ability to work well with people is essential. Familiarity with computer design software is required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Ability to communicate orally with customers, management, and other co-workers is crucial. Regular use

of the telephone and e-mail for communication is essential. Sitting for extended periods is common.

Hearing and vision within normal ranges is essential for normal conversations, to receive ordinary

information and to prepare or inspect documents.

No heavy lifting is expected. Exertion of up to 10 lbs. of force occasionally may be required. Good

manual dexterity for the use of common office equipment such as computer terminals, printers,

scanners, copiers, and FAX machines.

Good reasoning ability is required to solve a wide range of graphics problems. Able to apply geometry,

algebra and other analytics as required. Able to understand and utilize graphics designs, illustrations,

and engineering drawings to conduct business.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The job is performed indoors in a traditional office setting. Activities include extended periods

of sitting and extensive work at a computer monitor.

Title: PLC Programmer

Department: 600-Engineering

Reports To: Director of Operations

Effective Date: April 10, 2023

Position Summary:

The PLC programmer will design and install controller system software for our custom equipment and

innovative products. You will work onsite and travel to clients' locations, analyzing system

requirements, writing and installing custom programmable logic code, testing system efficiency, and

providing operational support for product solutions by extraktLAB.

To ensure success as the PLC programmer, you should have excellent knowledge of machine

mechanics, a logical approach, and the ability to work with minimal supervision. A skilled PLC

programmer should be able to easily identify and design a robust program fit for any mechanical or

electrical purpose.

PLC Programmer Responsibilities:

• Meetings with sales, production, engineering, and management to discuss our mechanical or

electrical automation needs.

• Drawing electrical or mechanical schematics to demonstrate how processes will work.

• Developing and installing machine programs using automation software and custom coding

languages.

• Determining machine automation test criteria before the final installation.

• Testing automated systems for efficiency, safety, and reliability.

• Troubleshooting system errors.

• Overseeing the successful installation of PLC programs.

• Documenting development processes.

• Ensure programming compliance to food and pharmaceutical standards (Gamp5)

• Providing clients with technical support.

• Other duties as assigned.

PLC Programmer Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in software engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a

similar field.

• PLC technical certification.

• At least 3 years’ experience as a PLC programmer.

• Electrical and mechanical engineering experience preferred.

• In-depth knowledge of manufacturing and mechanical processes.

• Knowledge of software design principals.

• Proficiency in CAD and AutoCAD software.

• Detailed knowledge of PLC automation software and coding languages.

• Ability to work with minimal supervision.

• Ability to travel when required.

Core Values:

• Superior Customer Experience

• Speed to Excellence

• Quality Finish

• Deliver the WOW

• Build the Next

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field; strong knowledge of mechanical engineering principles; proficiency in CAD software; problem-solving and analytical skills; ability to manage multiple tasks.

Job Summary

Nidec is the world's No. 1 comprehensive motor manufacturer handling "everything that spins and moves", miniature to gigantic. Nidec is a global enterprise comprised of over 300 subsidiaries/affiliates. We are a leading manufacturer of commercial motors, industrial motors, appliance motors, and controls. Our product line features a full line of high efficiency motors for industrial applications in water treatment, mining, oil and gas, and power generation, and for commercial applications such as pool and spa, condensers, cooling towers and large refrigeration units.

From keeping us comfortable in our homes to pumping clean water to making our cars more safe, electric motors are an indispensable part of our daily lives. At Nidec, our employees are on the forefront of developing new motor technologies. As we move deeper into the age of robotics, the impact of motors will only increase.

With over 140,000 employees stationed worldwide, Nidec continues to be a unique organization, and each location maintains its individual personality.

Whether driving locomotives, powering offshore platforms or keeping the lights on after a storm, Nidec electric power generation products impact the world on a daily basis. With over 1,000 employees in the Americas, we are moving forward with technology to solve our customers' electrical power needs for both prime and backup generation needs as the industry's leading manufacturer.

Job Summary

A rapidly growing division of Nidec Motor Corporation seeks candidates to fill an Engineer IV position, in St. Louis, MO. Nidec is the world's leading manufacturer of small precision motors, including motors used in hard disk drives and optical disk drives (including Blu-ray disk drives). The company has extended its focus beyond the information storage motor market to the industrial, home appliance, and automotive markets, where it sees high future growth potential. Nidec Motor Corporation is primarily engaged in the manufacture and sale of industrial and high efficiency motors in applications ranging from water treatment, mining, oil and gas, power generation, air conditioning, rooftop cooling towers and commercial refrigeration. Manufacturing facilities and technology centers are located in the United States, Mexico, China, India, and the UK.

Job Description

Responsibilities Include:

  • Conceive, Design, and analyze motor components for compliance to stated requirements.
  • Perform Finite Element Analysis (FEA) of new and existing designs to determine strength, temperature, and reliability characteristics.
  • Work with Project Manager and cross-functional teams to understand project goals, objectives, and to work toward meeting stated deliverables and schedule deadlines.
  • Create new component and assembly drawings per established Standards and Guidelines.
  • Create additional product specifications (e.g., manufacturing instructions, test procedures, material specs).
  • Utilize New Model and ECO process to create new BOM’s and revise established designs.
  • Work with procurement to obtain quotes and qualify suppliers, and to approve components per the FPA process.
  • Prepare reports and presentations for customers both internal/external.

Essential Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • BS Mechanical Engineering, MS Preferred
  • 2D/3D CAD (Pro/Engineer preferred, Solid Edge a plus)
  • Finite Element Analysis (FEA), utilizing Ansys (preferred) or similar software

    Mechanical Stress and Fatigue

    Fluid Dynamics

    Heat Transfer

    Rotor Dynamics

  • Microsoft Office Software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Proven Communication and Presentation skills

Additional Job Details

Additional Desirable Abilities or Experience

  • Design for Die Casting, Metal Forming, Machining, and Injection Molding
  • Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA)
  • Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)
  • Agency qualification testing (UL, CSA, IEEE)
  • Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T)
  • Tolerance Stack-Up Analysis (2D/3D). CETol software experience a plus

Basic Requirement All Professional Engineering Positions:
A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics;(d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR
B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.
2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.
3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program.
4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

GS-05 Basic Qualifications: Applicants who meet the basic requirements described in the individual occupational requirements are fully qualified for the specified entry grade of GS-05.

GS-07 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level or higher equivalency in the Federal service which includes work that involves:
1) Applying a basic understanding mechanical engineering theories, concepts, principles, and methods to all phases of mechanical systems design and computations;
2) Assisting in the preparation of engineering designs; and
3) Assisting in the inspection of engineering projects.
OR
Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: engineering technology, physics, or chemistry.
OR
Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:
1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses; OR
(2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum.; OR
3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/).
OR
Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages.

GS-12 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or higher equivalency in the Federal service which includes work that involves:
1) Preparing engineering designs for equipment, fixtures, and tooling required to support tracked vehicles.
2) Inspecting engineering projects for conformity with plans and specifications; and
3) Reviewing engineering drawings, plans and specification or cost estimates for engineering projects.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). Basic Requirement for Mechanical Engineer:

A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in architecture or in a related field that included 60 semester hours of course work in architecture or related disciplines of which at least (1) 30 semester hours were in architectural design, and (2) 6 semester hours were in each of the following: structural technology, properties of materials and methods of construction, and environmental control systems.

OR

B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the arts and sciences underlying professional architecture, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the architectural principles, methods, and techniques and their applications to the design and construction or improvement of buildings. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by at least one of the following: (1) Related Curriculum - Degree in architectural engineering provided the completed course work in architectural engineering provided knowledge, skills, and abilities substantially equivalent to those provided in the courses specified in statement A above, or (2) Experience: 1 year of experience in an architect's office or in architectural work for each year short of graduation from a program of study in architecture. In the absence of any college courses, 5 years of such experience is required. This experience must have demonstrated that you have acquired a thorough knowledge of the fundamental principles and theories of professional architecture.

Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes preparing engineering studies, designs, calculations, and analysis along with developing contract plans and specifications as required for the construction of the varied and complex civil works (water resources) projects.
This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11).

jobDescription:
Purpose  

The Mechanical Engineer supports Morgan City engineering activities for both small and large projects, as well as individual components of complex projects within Oceaneering's Subsea Robotics (SSR) and Offshore Projects Group (OPG). Typical work scopes include, but are not limited to, Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs), Intervention Workover Control Systems (IWOCS), ROV Workover Control Systems (RWOCS), ROV tooling, survey systems, installation and light construction projects, diving operations, inspection, maintenance, and repair (IMR) activities, and other assignments as directed by the Engineering Team Lead or Engineering Manager.

The Mechanical Engineer is responsible for supporting the full product and project lifecycle, including concept development, detailed design, engineering analysis, manufacturing support, testing, offshore operations, and field support. Key responsibilities include developing and reviewing engineering deliverables, performing calculations and analyses, conducting design reviews, supporting manufacturing and supply chain activities, troubleshooting technical issues and ensuring compliance with client requirements, applicable industry standards, and Oceaneering policies and procedures.

.

Work Location and Travel

  • Role provides the opportunity to work in hybrid environment, working both virtually and in office when required.

  • Position may require some travel including internationally and offshore.

  • Ability to travel offshore up to 20% of the time.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL

  • Ensure engineering activities are conducted in accordance with Oceaneering policies, processes, and safety requirements, with a strong focus on personnel and environmental safety. 

  • Ensure engineering deliverables comply with client requirements, contract specifications, and applicable industry standards including ISO, API, ANSI, DNV, AWS, and other relevant codes. 

  • Perform conceptual and detailed mechanical design, engineering analysis, and design verification for subsea equipment, tools, and systems. 

  • Design mechanical systems and equipment that interface with ROVs, subsea hardware, and related offshore systems. 

  • Develop and review engineering calculations, design packages, manufacturing drawings, assembly drawings, system layouts, and technical documentation. 

  • Prepare and review engineering specifications, procedures, work instructions, test procedures, user manuals, and related technical documents. 

  • Evaluate existing designs and implement improvements related to performance, reliability, manufacturability, safety, and cost. 

  • Select appropriate materials, coatings, cathodic protection systems, and corrosion mitigation solutions for subsea applications. 

  • Design pressure-containing and pressure-tolerant equipment, including systems requiring multiple electrical, hydraulic, or mechanical penetrations. 

  • Support engineering projects, technical proposals, bids, and project execution activities. 

  • Develop engineering cost estimates, schedules, work scopes, and progress reports. 

  • Communicate project status, technical issues, risks, and recommendations to customers, project teams, and management. 

  • Participate in internal and external design reviews and provide technical recommendations. 

  • Evaluate equipment, components, and suppliers and support technical sourcing and supplier qualification activities. 

  • Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, service, supply chain, project management, and field personnel to support successful project execution. 

  • Provide technical support for manufacturing, assembly, testing, troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair activities. 

  • Develop and execute test programs for factory acceptance testing (FAT), system integration testing (SIT), qualification testing, certification testing, and field trials. 

  • Attend and support FAT, SIT, offshore trials, commissioning activities, and customer demonstrations as required. 

  • Perform technical evaluations, root cause investigations, and corrective action development for field and operational issues. 

  • Support engineering change management, configuration control, and continuous improvement initiatives. 

  • Prepare and deliver technical presentations and training to internal and external stakeholders. 

  • Provide on-site oversight of subcontractors, offshore operations, installations, commissioning, and field support activities when required. 

  • Travel domestically and internationally, including offshore assignments, to support project execution, testing, commissioning, and customer requirements.

  • Participate in design risk assessments, FMEA reviews, and hazard analyses.

  • Support transition of new products into manufacturing through testing, documentation, training, and readiness activities.

 

Supervisory Responsibilities

 

This position has no supervisory responsibilities

 

Reporting Relationship

 

  • Reports to the Engineering Team Lead / Manager. 

 

Qualifications

REQUIRED

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Mechanical) or other related field. 

  • Minimum of two (2) years of engineering experience.

  • Must be able to obtain:

    • Transportation Workers Identification Card (TWIC)

    • Petroleum Education Council (PEC) Basic Training

    • Basic Offshore Safety Induction and Emergency Training (BOSIET)

 

DESIRED

  • Knowledge of GD&T, tolerance stack up analysis, and design for manufacturability 

  • Knowledge of ROV and/or subsea equipment design and engineering

  • Knowledge of basic hydraulic components and the ablity to read hydraulic schematics and P&IDs 

  • Working knowledge of Solidworks, AutoCAD, MathCAD, and ANSYS 

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

  • Good communication and presentation skills

 

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Characteristics

 

  • Ability to work in a team environment, remaining attentive to ideas, recognizing responsibilities, and actively participating with others to accomplish assignments and achieve desired goals.

  • Ability to write reports, business correspondence, procedures, and manuals. 

  • Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. 

  • Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

  • Gives and receives constructive feedback.

  • Ensures that others involved in a project or effort are kept informed about developments and plans.

  • Ensures that regular consistent communication takes place within area of responsibility.

 

Working Conditions

 

This position is considered 80% OFFICE WORK which is characterized as follows. 

  • Almost exclusively indoors during the day and occasionally at night.

  • Occasional exposure to airborne dust in the work place.

  • Work surface is stable (flat).

  • May, on occasion be sent out to the equipment yard (local or otherwise) or machine shop to participate in the assembly, FAT, or SIT of projects or other functions as needed.

 

This position is considered 20% OFFSHORE WORK which is characterized as follows.

  • Outdoors and indoors, day and night, as well as over/near water.

  • Requires work on or newar moving equipment and vibrating equipment

  • Frequently the humidity is above 90%, noise is over 85 decibels and the light is intense/glare

  • Potential exposure to open fire/flames/sparks

  • Constant exposure to airborne dust, fusmes, and gases

  • Work surface is stable, height is elevated

 

Physical Activity/Requirements 

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This position is considered LIGHT work.

 

8 or 3 years? [CR1]

Company

Oceaneering is a global provider of engineered services and products, primarily to the offshore energy industry. We develop products and services for use throughout the lifecycle of an offshore oilfield, from drilling to decommissioning. We operate the world's premier fleet of work class ROVs. Additionally, we are a leader in offshore oilfield maintenance services, umbilicals, subsea hardware, and tooling. We also use applied technology expertise to serve the defense, material handling, aerospace, science, and renewable energy industries.

jobDescription:
The Project Engineer has mastery of at least one core engineering principle and advanced knowledge of related engineering fields. The Project Engineer independently directs and technically manages engineering and design activities under the guidance of a Project Manager, and is responsible for tracking progress and technical adequacy of the design solution. The Project Engineer interacts with all OTECH departments as necessary to provide engineering support to OTECH manufacturing, integration, and test activities, and provides work leadership for lower level employees. 

Responsibilities

  • Develop and apply advanced engineering analytical and design methods, theories and research techniques, to complex engineering projects, culminating in practical, manufacturable, and serviceable designs

  • Lead and/or execute work ranging from working alone, working as part of a group, or working remotely, with minimal supervision.

  • Coordinate and supervise an interdisciplinary design team of engineers, designers, drafters, technical writers, and technicians.

  • Review progress and evaluate results of work accomplished by self and others.

  • Technically manage projects of moderate scope.

  • Estimate resource requirements to meet technical and scheduling objectives.

  • Review and approve the completion and implementation of technical products to meet the customer requirements.

  • Demonstrate excellent technical judgment, independent evaluation and innovative solutions to problems.

  • Write test procedures, conduct tests, compile and evaluate test data, and complete required documentation.

  • Interact with customer representatives to define and manage customer expectations.

  • Participate in Technical Working Groups to assess and improve ADTECH processes and capabilities.

  • Assist in bid and proposal efforts by providing cost estimations, technical approach definitions, and input to baseline schedule data.

  • Domestic and international travel, including shipboard operations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical or Ocean Engineering, from an accredited institution.

  • 5-10 years of practical technical experience in the engineering process, including concept development, analysis, design, drawing, integration and testing of complex mechanical and/or ocean deployed systems.

  • A minimum of three (3) years’ experience in the design of surface and/or subsea maritime equipment required.  Experience in the mechanical design, manufacturing and/or testing of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUV), Remote Controlled Vehicles (ROV) and/or Launch and Recovery Systems (LARS) preferred.

  • 2 or more years of management experience leading multidisciplinary design teams.

  • Responsible for producing significant portions of individual project mechanical designs

  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical groups and interact with customer representatives.

  • Proficiency in the application of current engineering software (i.e. SolidWorks, Matlab, etc), and Microsoft Office

  • Able to apply an advanced knowledge of the principles, practices and procedures of mechanical engineering and an understanding of related engineering fields that results in hardware designs that are robustly functional, practical, manufacturable, and serviceable in the field.

  • Work closely with electrical, software, and systems engineers, as well as other cooperative disciplines, to solve problems and constructively architect a working system.

  • Responsible and accountable for your results, working with considerable autonomy, but also knowing when to ask for assistance.

  • Ability to obtain a United States Government Department of Defense Security Clearance (active clearances preferred, but not prerequisite)

  • Desire to stretch and expand your talents, expertise, competency, and responsibilities.

 

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Employee benefits vary by role, however, may include Health and Wellness, Mental Health, Retirement Savings, Life and Disability, Paid Maternity and Parental Leave, Paid Time Off, Tuition Reimbursement, and an Employee Assistance Program.

 

Compensation $101,600.00 - $152,400.00

About Company

Oceaneering Aerospace and Defense Technologies (AdTech) delivers solutions that enable humans to work safely and effectively in harsh environments – from underwater to the outer reaches of space. Our innovative solutions support the development and application of practical, cost-effective systems that meet our customers’ challenges – from routine to extreme. Our experience and expertise across multiple industries uniquely positions us as a leader in the government, space, and maritime services markets. Our products and services meet the rigorous demands of the complex environments in which they operate, delivering results without compromising safety or reliability.

Company

Oceaneering is a global provider of engineered services and products, primarily to the offshore energy industry. We develop products and services for use throughout the lifecycle of an offshore oilfield, from drilling to decommissioning. We operate the world's premier fleet of work class ROVs. Additionally, we are a leader in offshore oilfield maintenance services, umbilicals, subsea hardware, and tooling. We also use applied technology expertise to serve the defense, material handling, aerospace, science, and renewable energy industries.

The Project Field Services Specialist provides on-site support to provide technical assistance with testing, assembly, installation, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, and troubleshooting of Oceaneering Technologies (OTECH) equipment on behalf of Oceaneering International. The Project Field Services Specialist is an onsite position located in Hanover, MD. The Project Field Services Specialists will have the ability to travel domestically and overseas up to 20% of the year. 

Responsibilities

  • Perform a variety of fundamental field services tasks with minimal supervision of a senior level engineer; involved in the installation, operation, testing, and maintenance of electro-mechanical equipment and systems. 
  • Interface with all phases of assembly and manufacturing; ensure input at an early stage for appropriate system design with supervision. 
  • Assists in developing manufacturing and installation cost-benefit analysis input. 
  • Assist in conducting research and reference reading to assist programs in obtaining technical information and keeping informed of currently approved standards, codes, and procedures applied to various engineering disciplines. 
  • Assist with generating sections of design specifications of more complex projects or complete specifications of less complex projects. 
  • Augment engineering process at design reviews with manufacturing / field experience. 
  • Assist in the red-lining of drawing packages to reflect “as-Built” status of equipment.
  • Plan and carry out successive engineering steps and resolve technical problems by standard practices and techniques such as tolerance studies and design calculations. 
  • Provide resolution to manufacturing problems. 
  • Troubleshoot and repair electro-mechanical systems. 
  • Troubleshoot and repair fiberoptic systems. 
  • Conduct laboratory investigations and root cause analyses on equipment or systems. 
  • Support projects with limited scope, or parts of more complex projects with detailed instructions on the intent and scope of the documents to be prepared. 
  • Support projects with limited logistics support. 
  • Assist in creation / updates of maintenance manuals, documents, and drawings.  
  • Proficient with ANSI Y14.5, AutoCAD, SolidWorks, AWS D1.1,2
  • Assist in preparation of reports, correspondence, or technical studies. 
  • Prepare, deliver, and submit technical presentations for in-process design and review meetings. 
  • Perform all other position-related duties as assigned or requested. 
  • Some travel will be required, including sporadic offshore work, extended workdays and work weeks, with limited communications for continuous (1-2 months) periods of time. 
  • Additional duties as assigned. 

Supervisory Responsibilities 

  • This position has no supervisory responsibilities. 

Qualifications

REQUIRED 

  • Advanced knowledge of applicable Subsea & Seabed Warfare (SSW) engineering concepts, principles, and familiarity with related engineering fields. 
  • Minimum 5-9 years of experience in field operations including fabrication, assembly, installation and testing of SSW electro-mechanical systems, including hydraulics, propulsion, manipulator, fiber optic, navigation, and subsea environmental sensing equipment. 
  • Professional knowledge of applicable engineering concepts and principles and a familiarity with related engineering fields. 
  • Practical knowledge of test methods and practices sufficient to perform routine to more complex engineering procedures and to prepare or make minor modifications of standard test procedures or test equipment work instructions.  
  • Experience with preparation of progress reports, job completion estimates, and cost estimating essential. 
  • Well versed with ANSI Y14.5, AutoCAD, SolidWorks, AWS D1.1,2 
  • Able to read / understand Engineering electrical and mechanical schematics / drawings.  
  • Current Top Secret security clearance. 

 

DESIRED 

  • SCI clearance and Counterintelligence (CI) polygraph. 
  • Bachelor's degree or greater in related field. Equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of a degree. 
  • Experience directly related to construction, installation, testing, and maintenance of undersea equipment. 

 

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Employee benefits vary by role, however, may include Health and Wellness, Mental Health, Retirement Savings, Life and Disability, Paid Maternity and Parental Leave, Paid Time Off, Tuition Reimbursement, and an Employee Assistance Program.

Job Description:

ABOUT TTI

Techtronic Industries is a fast-growing world leader in Power Tools, Accessories, Hand Tools, Outdoor Power Equipment, and Floor Care for Do-It-Yourself (DIY), professional and industrial users in the home improvement, repair, maintenance, construction, and infrastructure industries. The Company is committed to accelerating the transformation of these industries through superior environmentally friendly cordless technology. At TTI Anderson, our brand RYOBI is recognized worldwide for its deep heritage and cordless product platform of superior quality, outstanding performance, safety, productivity, and compelling innovation.

 

JOB SUMMARY

The Mechanical Engineer as part of the Advanced Engineering team is a technical lead with responsibilities of developing, analyzing, and maturing complex mechanical systems for next-generation tools. This role focuses on transforming early concepts and emerging technologies into robust, feasible mechanical solutions through calculations, analysis, prototyping, and testing. The Advanced Engineering team is highly collaborative, deeply hands-on, and driven by curiosity and learning as we develop new and innovative consumer power tool products.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES / SKILLS

  • Own mechanical feasibility, performance validation, and technical risk reduction for advanced projects
  • Develop and evaluate mechanisms, structures, and integrated systems using analysis and physical testing
  • Translate early concepts into technically mature designs suitable for transition into product development
  • Build, test, and iterate functional prototypes to validate durability, performance, and manufacturability
  • Determine system requirements, user operation methods, and design trade-offs
  • Partner with Marketing, Engineering, Industrial Design, and other cross-functional teams to ensure stakeholder alignment and a balanced technical solution
  • Communicate technical findings, risks, and recommendations clearly to engineering leadership and other stakeholders

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • B.S. in Mechanical or related Engineering disciplines; advanced degree a plus
  • Proficiency with 3D CAD and GD&T
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and hands-on attitude
  • Mechanical design fundamentals with related knowledge in mechanisms, gear design, structures, engineering materials, and manufacturing processes associated with those materials
  • Experience building prototypes, developing test plans, and defining acceptance criteria
  • Proven ability to work proactively and take ownership
  • Ability to work on multiple projects in various stages of development simultaneously
  • Experience in Microsoft Office programs, especially Excel and Powerpoint
  • Ability to use advanced tools (FEA, CFD, AI/ML) a plus
  • Experience with measurement equipment (o-scope, vibration, sound) a plus
  • Experience with embedded electronics and controls a plus
  • undefinedSoftwareMS Office, Solidworks, NX, Ansys Mechanical, Discovery, KISSsoft

About Us

TTI is a world-class leader in design, manufacturing and marketing of Power Tools, Hand Tools, Outdoor Power Equipment, and Floor Care and Appliances for consumers, professional and industrial users in the home improvement, repair and construction industries. Our unrelenting strategic focus on Powerful Brands, Innovative Products, Operational Excellence and Exceptional People drives our culture.

TTI was founded by Mr. Horst Julius Pudwill and Prof. Roy Chi Ping Chung BBS JP in 1985, yet the history of TTI's unique and growing portfolio of world-famous brands stretches back at least one hundred and fifty years. Through a clear and consistent strategy of acquiring and developing established brands, TTI has grown to become a clear market leader in power tools, outdoor power equipment, hand tools and floor care appliances worldwide. TTI is proud of its own history, and proud, too, of the huge legacy of tradition and excellence that we have inherited from the brands that make up our Company today.

TTI actively promotes a strong corporate culture of respect and ethical integrity. Our Values are our beliefs, principles and standards that do not change over time. Description

Kitchell is seeking an experienced Mechanical Engineer to join our Southern California region in San Diego and build a long-term career at one of the most innovative and growth-oriented Construction Services companies in the United States.

 

Overview

As a Mechanical Engineer, you will provide mechanical and plumbing engineering expertise to support project design, construction, and delivery. You will work closely with internal teams, clients, consultants, architects, and contractors to develop effective solutions that meet project requirements, applicable codes and standards, and Kitchell’s commitment to quality.

This position will support a variety of projects and will be responsible for providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle, from design development and documentation through construction administration and closeout. The ideal candidate will bring strong mechanical engineering fundamentals, sound judgment, and the ability to collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide mechanical and plumbing engineering expertise and technical support for designated projects.
  • Develop, review, and document mechanical and plumbing systems in accordance with project requirements, applicable codes, and industry standards.
  • Communicate project intent clearly and effectively, ensuring client requirements and project goals are incorporated into design solutions.
  • Review project documents, drawings, specifications, calculations, and technical reports for accuracy, quality, and compliance.
  • Coordinate mechanical and plumbing systems with architectural, structural, electrical, and other building systems.
  • Provide technical support during construction, including responding to RFIs, reviewing submittals, evaluating proposed changes, and assisting with resolution of field issues.
  • Visit project sites as needed to observe existing and ongoing construction conditions and provide engineering expertise and recommendations.
  • Identify potential design, constructability, coordination, and project risks and communicate concerns to the appropriate project leadership.
  • Participate in project meetings with clients, consultants, contractors, and internal teams.
  • Assist with project planning, work plans, schedules, budgets, and deliverables as needed.
  • Monitor project requirements and deliverables to help ensure work is completed accurately, on time, and within established budgets.
  • Support the development of technical approaches, scopes of work, and fee estimates for assigned projects.
  • Assist with proposals, presentations, and other technical marketing materials as requested.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with clients, consultants, contractors, and internal teams.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to less experienced engineering staff as appropriate.
  • Stay current with applicable building codes, regulations, industry standards, and emerging mechanical engineering practices.

Requirements

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university in mechanical engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience required.
  • 5+ years of relevant mechanical engineering experience preferred.
  • Experience with the design and documentation of mechanical and plumbing systems for commercial, institutional, civic, healthcare, education, public safety, or similar facilities preferred.
  • Experience supporting projects through design and construction phases preferred.
  • Experience working with public sector projects is a plus.

 

Knowledge and Skills

  • Demonstrated experience designing, documenting, and coordinating mechanical and plumbing systems.
  • Strong understanding of mechanical engineering principles, building systems, applicable codes, and industry standards.
  • Proficiency with Revit, Bluebeam, Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience with Trane TRACE, Title 24 compliance software, or similar engineering and energy analysis tools preferred.
  • Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, calculations, and other technical data to identify and solve complex problems.
  • Ability to evaluate existing conditions and develop practical, constructible engineering solutions.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with clients, consultants, contractors, and internal teams.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple assignments and meet project deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively as part of a multidisciplinary project team.
  • Adaptable under pressure and capable of effectively managing change, delays, and unexpected project conditions.
  • Demonstrated commitment to quality and attention to detail.

 

Licenses and Certifications

  • State of California Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer in Training (EIT) certification is preferred.
  • A valid driver’s license with an acceptable motor vehicle record, free from suspensions or restrictions, is required.

 

Travel Requirement

This position is office based in the San Diego, CA Regional Office. Travel to project sites, client meetings, and other locations is required based on project needs.

 

Work Environment

While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works in an office environment and frequently works in a construction environment. Conditions may occasionally include exposure to outdoor elements, hot and cold temperatures, wet conditions, noise, atmospheric conditions, and cramped quarters. The noise level in the work environment is regularly moderate and occasionally loud. When visiting active construction sites, appropriate personal protective equipment may be required.

 

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to regularly sit, talk, listen, and use hands to finger, feel, and handle; frequently stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms; and occasionally climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Must frequently lift and/or move up to 5 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.

Job Description:

Mechanical Design Engineer - Advanced Engineering

 

Applicants must currently hold a U.S. work-authorized status that supports long-term employment and a pathway to permanent residency. Candidates in visitor, student, exchange, treaty investor/trader, or other temporary statuses that do not readily support employment-based permanent residency will not be considered.


Techtronic Industries, the world leader in cordless technology across Outdoor Power Equipment, Power Tools, Floor Care Appliances, and Accessories, is seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer for the Ryobi Outdoor Products Advanced Engineering team at our Innovation Center in Anderson, SC.

This role is ideal for a hands-on mechanical engineer who enjoys turning ambiguous product ideas into working, tested, manufacturable solutions before they enter formal product development. You will help develop future outdoor power equipment technologies by converting early concepts into validated mechanical systems that improve performance, durability, user experience, and manufacturability.


Advanced Engineering operates upstream of traditional new product development. The team explores new mechanisms, proves out key technical assumptions, reduces risk through analysis, prototyping, and testing, and transitions mature concepts to product development teams.

The Advanced Engineering team is highly collaborative, deeply hands-on, and driven by curiosity, learning, and practical problem solving as we develop innovative outdoor products that create real value for our customers.


What You’ll Do:

  • Develop advanced mechanical concepts for next-generation outdoor power equipment and battery-powered outdoor products
  • Create mechanisms, structures, and integrated assemblies that balance performance, durability, manufacturability, cost, and user experience
  • Use first-principles analysis, hand calculations, simulation, benchmarking, and test data to guide design decisions
  • Build, test, and iterate functional prototypes to quickly validate key assumptions, identify risks, and mature concepts
  • Define system requirements, user operation methods, design trade-offs, and acceptance criteria for advanced mechanical systems
  • Translate early concepts into robust, production-minded designs that can be handed off to downstream engineering teams
  • Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Industrial Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and other cross-functional teams to develop balanced technical solutions
  • Communicate technical findings, risks, recommendations, and next steps clearly to engineering leadership and project stakeholders
  • Support project planning by contributing to milestone definition, schedule inputs, prototype needs, and technical risk assessments

 

Required Qualifications:

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline
  • 3+ years of mechanical design experience in product development, advanced engineering, concept maturation, or innovation-focused roles
  • Strong proficiency with 3D CAD, such as NX, SolidWorks, or similar tools
  • Strong mechanical design fundamentals, including mechanisms, structures, engineering materials, manufacturing processes, and tolerance considerations
  • Experience building prototypes, developing test plans, evaluating results, and using data to improve designs
  • Ability to manage multiple projects or concepts at different stages of maturity
  • Ability to work with a high degree of autonomy, ownership, curiosity, and proactivity
  • Willingness to travel approximately 5-10%, including domestic and international travel as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience designing consumer products, outdoor power equipment, power tools, or similar high-volume mechanical products
  • Experience using FEA, CFD, dynamic simulation, gear design tools, or other advanced analysis methods to guide product design
  • Experience with rapid prototyping across multiple materials and processes
  • Familiarity with vibration, sound, airflow, thermal, durability, or performance testing
  • Familiarity with integrated electrical and mechanical systems, including motors, batteries, sensors, and control interfaces
  • Advanced degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

Tools & Technologies:
Candidates should be comfortable using modern engineering tools to develop, analyze, communicate, and validate mechanical designs.

Summary

The Mechanical Engineer designs, specifies, and validates the mechanical hardware and systems the plant runs on. This covers custom fabrication and change parts, modifications to existing equipment, conveyance and material handling, machine guarding, drive systems, and the mechanical utilities that support production.

Where the Manufacturing Engineer defines how a product is made, this role defines the physical means of making it and is accountable for whether that hardware is sound, sanitary, serviceable, and safe. A design that runs but cannot be cleaned, cannot be maintained, or cannot be reproduced from the drawing has not met the standard.

Duties and Responsibilities

Mechanical Design and Fabrication

•      Produce three dimensional models and detailed fabrication drawings for change parts, tooling, fixtures, guards, transitions, chutes, hoppers, frames, and platforms, with tolerances and finishes specified rather than left to the fabricator.

•      Perform the engineering calculations that support a design, including loads, stress, deflection, fatigue, torque, drive sizing, and power transmission selection.

•      Select materials and finishes appropriate to a food environment, accounting for product contact, cleaning chemistry, temperature, corrosion, and wear.

•      Apply sanitary design principles to all custom fabrication, including radii, surface finish, drainability, avoidance of crevices and hollow bodies, and appropriate fastener and joint selection.

•      Manage fabrication through internal shop resources and outside vendors, including drawing release, quoting, progress review, inspection, and acceptance of finished work.

•      Maintain drawing control, revision history, and bills of material so a part can be reordered years later without being reverse engineered.

Equipment Modification and Machine Systems

•      Design and validate modifications to existing production equipment, and assess the effect of any modification on machine safety, sanitary status, warranty, and original equipment manufacturer support before it is made.

•      Design and lay out conveyance and material handling systems, including transfers, accumulation, elevation changes, and product handling that protects product integrity.

•      Size and select drive components including motors, gear reducers, belts, chains, bearings, and couplings, and document the basis of selection.

•      Design machine guarding and access to the applicable safety standard, and support machine safety risk assessments.

•      Design pneumatic and hydraulic circuits and specify components for the application and the environment.

•      Design for maintainability, so that wear parts can be reached, serviced, and replaced without disassembling unrelated equipment.

Mechanical Utilities and Facility Systems

•      Provide engineering support for mechanical utility systems including refrigeration, steam and condensate, compressed air, process water, wastewater, and heating and ventilation.

•      Perform load, capacity, and sizing calculations for utility systems and distribution, and identify where capacity constrains production or where a system is oversized and wasteful.

•      Specify piping, valves, pumps, and heat transfer equipment appropriate to the service, including sanitary service where product contact applies.

•      Support Process Safety Management activities where ammonia refrigeration is present, including process hazard analysis, mechanical integrity, and management of change.

Asset Integrity and Reliability Engineering

•      Analyze mechanical component failures to determine the mechanism, including wear, fatigue, misalignment, lubrication, overload, or material selection, and correct the design or specification rather than reordering the same part.

•      Specify predictive and condition monitoring strategy for mechanical assets, including vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis, and alignment standards.

•      Engineer the critical spare parts strategy, including interchangeability, standardization across equipment and across sites, and identification of single source risk.

•      Assess equipment condition and remaining life, and develop replacement and rebuild recommendations with a supporting technical and financial case.

Standards, Documentation, and Technical Support

•      Develop and maintain mechanical engineering standards for design, materials, fasteners, guarding, and documentation, so work is consistent across projects and across sites.

•      Maintain accurate mechanical documentation including assembly drawings, part drawings, layouts, and equipment files.

•      Provide engineering support to Maintenance on mechanical problems that exceed routine repair, and to Manufacturing Engineering on the hardware requirements of process and capital work.

•      Support internal, customer, regulatory, and third party audits by producing design documentation and technical justification on request.

•      Provide technical direction to designers, drafters, fabricators, and outside vendors, and verify their work against the specification.

•      Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

Required

•      Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent demonstrated design engineering capability and experience.

•      Three or more years of mechanical design experience in a manufacturing environment.

•      Demonstrated proficiency in three dimensional computer aided design and in producing complete, dimensioned, buildable fabrication drawings.

•      Working knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, fits, and surface finish specification.

•      Ability to perform and document the engineering calculations that justify a design, and to state the assumptions behind them.

•      Working knowledge of materials, coatings, and elastomers suitable for food contact and washdown service.

•      Working knowledge of power transmission and drive component selection.

•      Working knowledge of machine safety standards, guarding design, and risk assessment.

•      Ability to work with fabrication shops and vendors, including reading their constraints back into the design.

•      Willingness to be present on the floor and on off shifts during installation, trials, and startup, since a design is proven at the machine and not at the desk.

Preferred

•      Experience with SolidWorks.

•      Familiarity with 3-A Sanitary Standards and with ASME BPE requirements.

•      Experience with ammonia refrigeration systems and Process Safety Management requirements.

•      Vibration analysis, alignment, or other predictive maintenance certification or training.

•      Working knowledge of welding and fabrication processes sufficient to design for the shop that will build it.

•      Familiarity with applicable pressure piping and pressure vessel codes.

•      Professional Engineer license, or progress toward it.

•      Bilingual in English and Spanish.

Expectations and Measures of Success

Performance in this role is measured by whether the hardware works, holds up, and can be lived with. The following describe what success looks like.

•      Designs install and run as intended, without field rework to make them fit or function.

•      Custom fabrication cleans, drains, and passes sanitation and audit scrutiny.

•      Drawings and bills of material are complete and current, so parts can be reordered or rebuilt from the documentation alone.

•      Mechanical failures are analyzed and designed out rather than replaced repeatedly.

•      Spare parts complexity decreases over time through standardization across equipment and across sites.

•      Maintenance regards the designs as serviceable, which is a judgment they make and not one this role can assert.

Supervisory Responsibility

Typically none. This role provides technical direction to designers, drafters, fabrication shop personnel, vendors, and contractors without formal supervisory authority. Some sites may assign designers, engineering technicians, co ops, or interns to this position.

Work Environment

This role divides time between an office or design environment, the maintenance and fabrication shop, and the production floor of a food manufacturing facility. On the floor and in the shop, the employee is exposed to moving mechanical parts, welding and grinding operations, wet and slippery surfaces, cleaning chemicals, and loud noise requiring hearing protection, in refrigerated, ambient, or mixed temperature areas depending on the site. Time on the floor increases substantially during installation, trials, commissioning, and shutdowns. Presence on off shifts, weekends, and during planned shutdowns is expected, since installation work occurs outside of normal production hours.

jobDescription:
THE POSITION

Are you prepared to elevate complex systems through expert mechanical guidance? As a Mechanical Engineer Consultant with the Department of Corrections, you will take the lead on specialized mechanical engineering work that supports institutional infrastructure. This position gives you the chance to analyze designs, review project details, and recommend improvements based on expert judgment. You will work closely with engineers, contractors, and facility staff to ensure systems meet high standards. Become part of a team that values innovation, precision, and strong professional insight!

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position provides advanced mechanical engineering guidance through design preparation, project review, and technical consultation for statewide correctional facilities. It requires professional engineering judgment to evaluate systems, recommend solutions, and ensure compliance with standards. As a Mechanical Engineer Consultant, you will perform the following duties:

  • Design Development: Create detailed mechanical specifications, design data, and CAD drawings for construction projects
  • Site Evaluation: Conduct field surveys, gather relevant information, and prepare reports with observations and cost recommendations
  • Interdisciplinary Coordination: Work with internal staff, external professionals, and code officials during project planning and development
  • Technical Review: Assess mechanical drawings, estimates, and design reports and approve or recommend revisions
  • Construction Oversight: Inspect project sites to verify compliance with design standards and resolve mechanical concerns
  • Problem Resolution: Develop solutions for operational, maintenance, or design issues using advanced engineering principles


Interested in learning more? Additional details regarding this position can be found in the position description.


Work Schedule and Additional Information:

  • Full-time employment, 37.5 hours per week
  • Work hours are 7:30 AM to 3:30 PM, Monday - Friday, with a 30-minute lunch.
  • Telework: You may have the opportunity to work from home (telework) part-time up to 3 days per week after the initial 6-month training period. During the training period, you must report in person to 1920 Technology Parkway, Mechanicsburg. In order to telework, you must have a securely configured high-speed internet connection and work from an approved location inside Pennsylvania. If you are unable to telework, you will have the option to report to the headquarters office in Mechanicsburg, PA. The ability to telework is subject to change at any time. Additional details may be provided during the interview.
  • Travel is required.
  • Salary: In some cases, the starting salary may be non-negotiable. 
  • Employees with the required certification or license may be eligible to receive a lump sum payment at the time of hire and each time the certification or license is renewed.

You will receive further communication regarding this position via email. Check your email, including spam/junk folders, for these notices.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to become the Main Injector/Recycler (MI/RR) Primary Machine Engineer who is a collaborator by nature and who seeks out the latest technology and tools to design, fabricate, test, install and operate components and systems for our particle accelerators.

What your day-to-day as a Mechanical Engineer at Fermilab will look like:

  • You will serve as Primary Machine Engineer for the MI/RR machines and work with MI/RR machine stakeholders and scientists in the planning, implementation, and documentation of the installation of upgrades and repairs to the mechanical systems that support this accelerator. Oversee engineers, drafter/designers and technicians in their tasks. 

  • Provide support to future accelerators such as PIP-II and LBNF in the mechanical design, analysis, fabrication/construction, and installation of devices and equipment.

  • Utilize fundamental engineering concepts and principles to complete assignments and develop familiarization with the Laboratory’s method of project engineering, from the design stage through review, procurement, fabrication, installation, test and operation.

  • Participate in and leading efforts involving general mechanical-system design, mechanical stress analysis, and thermal analysis.

  • Designing and planning the lifting/rigging of heavy components which will involve material handling equipment and techniques.

  • Overseeing and directing the activities of early-career engineers, technicians, and drafters/designers on their projects.

  • Direct the activities of co-op engineering students and interns on his/her projects.

  • Abide by and be responsible for performing all duties in accordance with all environmental, health and safety regulations and practices pertinent to this position. 

Skills and Attributes for Success:

  • Bachelor’s in an applicable Engineering discipline from an ABET accredited institution with 6+ years of engineering experience, or a Master’s in an applicable Engineering discipline from an ABET accredited institution with 4+ years of engineering experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate expectations clearly using verbal and written practices with customers / stakeholders and with team members

  • Demonstrated ability to lead a team in a project (technical or non-technical) and installation activities

  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively under the requirements of schedules and shifting priorities

  • Demonstrated ability to perform mechanical stress and deflection calculations 

  • Demonstrated ability to create and read mechanical drawings 

  • Demonstrated knowledge of machine shop practices and techniques for fabricating complex and intricate hardware

  • Must have strong computing skills including preparing and documenting engineering calculations, creating 3D models and 2D drawings using CAD software, FEA analyses, data presentation, and project management activities (cost estimates, schedules)

  • Experience with design, assembly and operation of high and ultra-high vacuum systems is desirable

  • Knowledge of welding and brazing practices (e.g. TIG, MIG and electron beam welding process, oven brazing) as related to manufacturing and fabrication of structures is desirable

  • Knowledge of materials, metallurgy and radiation damage of materials is desirable

  • Knowledge in the design and planning of lifting/rigging of heavy components which involve material handling of equipment and techniques is desirable

  • Use of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing on drawings is desirable 

  • Planning and implementing preventative maintenance programs for a system’s equipment is desirable

  • Skills in Siemens Teamcenter and NX is desirable

  • Skills in ANSYS or NASTRAN is desirable

  • Experience in specifying, designing, fabrication, and operations of robotics systems is desirable

About the Role:


The Mechanical Support Department of the Accelerator Division within Fermilab is seeking a Mechanical Thermal Fluids Engineer.  Under general directions, this individual will be responsible for planning, researching, and developing large/ major engineering projects.  They will lead and contribute to areas such as design, procurement, manufacture, installation, testing, and initial operation of thermal systems in compliance with all applicable local, state, and federal regulations, requirements, and standards, and all Department of Energy (DOE) orders.  Responsibilities will also include the estimation of manpower, work scheduling, coordinating and directing or managing technicians and other engineers as assigned.  Will review progress and evaluate results.

What your day-to-day as a Thermal Fluids Mechanical Engineer at Fermilab will look like:

  • Utilize fundamental mechanical engineering concepts and principles to complete assignments and develop familiarization with the Laboratory’s method of project engineering, from the design stage through review, procurement, fabrication, installation, test, and operation.
  • Perform mechanical design, analysis, specification, and construction of fluid cooling piping systems that support the operation of the accelerator complex, including the temperature control of beamline components such as magnets, collimators, RF cavities, beam instrumentation, high-powered targets, kickers, and associated beam components.
  • Participate in and lead efforts related to thermal-fluid system design, piping system fluid flow analysis, and heat transfer analysis.
  • Learn the operations of existing accelerator fluids systems and provide operations engineering support by troubleshooting system issues and designing upgrades to existing systems to improve their reliability.
  • Participate in the design of compressible and incompressible thermal fluids systems to support the accelerator.
  • Write fabrication specifications that involve welding, brazing, bonding, and soldering techniques with materials such as aluminum, stainless steels, copper, brass, PVC, CPVC, PVDF etc. 
  • Work in a team environment and under the supervision of a senior engineer.
  • Be responsible for directing the activities of drafters, designers, technicians, and skilled trades on their projects.
  • Occasionally direct the activities of co-op engineering students and interns on their projects.
  • Communicate with outside vendors, contractors, and fabricators verbally and through written specifications and engineering drawings.
  • Abide by and be responsible for performing all duties in accordance with all environmental, health and safety regulations and practices pertinent to this position. 

Skills and Attributes for Success:

  • Bachelor’s in an applicable Engineering discipline from an ABET accredited institution with 4+ years of engineering experience, or a Master’s or PhD in an applicable Engineering discipline from an ABET accredited institution with 2+ years of engineering experience.


Applicable Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate expectations clearly using verbal and written practices with customers / stakeholders, and with team members.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively under the requirements of schedules and shifting priorities.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, piping network calculations, and engineering mechanics calculations including statics, stress, strain, and deflection. 
  • Basic understanding of electrical engineering concepts such as current, voltages, resistance, frequencies, and speed requirements. 
  • Demonstrated ability to create and read mechanical drawings, including piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&ID) and process piping flow schematics.
  • Demonstrated ability in performing mass and energy balance calculation on various hydraulic and heat transfer components.
  • Demonstrated ability in performing heat transfer calculations to size heat exchangers.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of machine shop practices and techniques.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of piping flexibility analysis is desirable.
  • Must have strong computing skills including preparing and documenting engineering calculations, creating 3D models and 2D drawings using CAD software data presentation, and project management activities (cost estimates, schedules).
  • Familiarity of CAD software for the creation of piping fluid flow network systems is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to creatively solve engineering problems and troubleshoot operational issues.
  • Knowledge of welding and brazing practices (e.g., TIG, MIG and torch brazing) as related to manufacturing and fabrication of piping is desirable.
  • Knowledge of materials, metallurgy, and radiation damage of materials is desirable.
  • Knowledge of codes and standards such as ASME, AISC, CGI, API and ANSI/ASME pressure vessel and piping codes is desirable.
  • Use of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing on drawings per ASME Y14.5 is desirable. 
  • Skills or experience in AFT Fathom, AFT Arrow, and ANSYS Workbench are desirable.
  • Skills or experience in AutoCAD Plant are desirable.
