Job Description

As a Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer here at Honeywell, you will lead initiatives to optimize and innovate manufacturing processes, driving operational excellence and efficiency. You will leverage your expertise to implement advanced manufacturing strategies and technologies that enhance productivity and product quality.

The Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer will be responsible for developing, implementing, validating, maintaining, and improving manufacturing processes across machining, assembly, test, fabrication, and engineered plastics operations. This role supports the production of centrifugal pump components, including machined metallic components and ANSIMAG sealless magnetic-drive non-metallic product lines with molded ETFE wetted components.

The successful candidate will lead continuous improvement, cost reduction, quality improvement, and production support initiatives by partnering closely with shop-floor technicians, operators, supervisors, Product Engineering, Planning, Quality, Supply Chain, and management. This is a day-shift, salaried position that works under limited supervision and reports to the Shop Supervisor / Manager. You’ll work out of our Arvada, CO location on an On-site work schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, validate, maintain, and improve manufacturing processes for assigned areas, including machining, assembly, test, kit fabrication, engineered plastic parts, insert molded parts, and injection molded fabrication processes
  • Create, revise, and maintain NC programs, fixturing, tooling, standard work, process sketches, in-process inspection plans, process notes, assembly instructions, process instructions, test instructions, bills of material, labor routings, and shop-floor routings
  • Evaluate alternative plastic resins, manufacturing methods, equipment, tooling, and process improvements to support cost reduction, manufacturability, quality, and product performance
  • Improve manufacturing efficiency by analyzing workflow, production flow, assembly methods, space requirements, equipment layout, process capability, and production volume while maintaining and improving quality standards
  • Lead analysis of manufacturing costs in support of strategic make/buy decisions, accurate standard costing, capital investment justification, and cost-reduction initiatives
  • Participate in production traceability and configuration control, including changes and corrections to bills of material, routings, technical work instructions, NC programs, inspection plans, and test plans
  • Support non-conforming material disposition, root cause analysis, customer complaint investigations, internal issue resolution, third-party audit responses, and corrective action implementation
  • Lead and support Lean, Six Sigma, TPM, and 5S initiatives to eliminate waste, reduce variation, remove bottlenecks, and improve manufacturing, assembly, test, and fabrication processes
  • Coordinate with Manufacturing Supervision, operators, technicians, engineers, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, and management to resolve production issues and improve manufacturing capabilities
  • Support injection molding training and develop working knowledge of internal processes, customer specifications, and best practices for sealless magnetic-drive pump products
  • Identify, justify, research, quote, procure, test, and implement capital equipment investments, including preparation of Capital Authorization Requests as needed

Qualifications

You Must Have:

  • 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing engineering or similar role within a manufacturing environment
  • 3+ years of experience with CAD/CAM software; Siemens NX preferred
  • 3+ years of experience in machining, metal cutting, plastics manufacturing, injection molding, or related production environment
  • Experience with varied metallurgies such as carbon steel, stainless steel alloys, titanium, Hastelloy, and aluminum preferred
  • Experience supporting engineered plastic components, molded ETFE components, insert molded parts, or injection molded fabrication processes preferred
  • Ability to lift 35 pounds unassisted

We Value

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field
  • Lean Six Sigma experience, APICS certification, or demonstrated experience applying lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies
  • Experience with VPP sites, EH&S programs, TPM, 6S, ISO standard work, and formal safety management practices
  • Experience managing multi-shift or 24-hour machine shop operations
  • Familiarity with various production processes, including plastic molding, tooling, assembly, and test
  • Strong communication skills, reading, listening, and talking are common

Job Title: Manufacturing EngineerJob Description

The Manufacturing Engineer will support an aerospace sheet metal forming facility in Chandler, AZ by developing efficient, cost-effective manufacturing processes for complex sheet metal components. The role focuses on translating engineering designs, CAD models, specifications, and purchase order requirements into robust production methods, tooling, and process plans that achieve high quality at the lowest practical cost. The engineer will lead and support new product introduction, continuous improvement, and customer liaison activities within an AS9100-regulated environment.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct research and development projects related to the design and development of new products and services, particularly in aerospace sheet metal manufacturing.
  • Contribute to and follow project plans for new product development orders, ensuring tasks progress on schedule and meet technical and quality requirements.
  • Prepare detailed shop operation sketches, instruction sheets, bills of materials, tool orders, and other process documentation to define the most cost-effective integrated fabrication and inspection methods.
  • Review customer documentation and specifications and ensure that all manufacturing plans, routings, and process instructions fully reflect customer requirements.
  • Design and create complete tooling and fixturing drawings using CAD software to support sheet metal fabrication processes, and develop work orders and plans to fabricate tooling either in-house or through outside suppliers.
  • Serve as an engineering liaison with customers, maintaining specific knowledge of customer quality requirements and specifications and communicating effectively to address technical issues and inquiries.
  • Resolve implementation and process problems on the shop floor and respond quickly to liaison requests related to manufacturing issues.
  • Provide technical assistance to shop and inspection personnel, perform MRB (Material Review Board) dispositions, and conduct investigations to resolve quality and process problems.
  • Maintain close working relationships with all departments and individuals involved in assigned projects and coordinate with customer representatives as necessary to support program success.
  • Monitor manufacturing cell metrics, including gross margin, scrap, rework, 5S, and other continuous improvement indicators, and identify improvement opportunities with actionable plans to address them.
  • Conduct special studies to develop and establish standard hours, cost data, and other metrics to support cost reduction and productivity improvement initiatives.
  • Consult with clients, vendors, and other stakeholders to discuss and formulate estimates, clarify requirements, and resolve technical or process issues.
  • Create and maintain process layouts and routings, ensuring accurate and efficient workflow definitions for 3–7 years of experience in this area.
  • Apply GD&T principles in daily work to ensure accurate interpretation and communication of dimensional and tolerance requirements on drawings and process documents.
  • Use lean tools such as Six Sigma and value stream mapping (VSM) to identify and implement process improvements across manufacturing cells.
  • Support or participate in multi-axis programming activities, such as laser cutting or other CNC processes, where applicable.
  • Perform all other related duties as assigned to support production, engineering, and continuous improvement objectives.

Essential Skills

  • Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Engineering, or at least seven (7) years of related experience, or a combination of education and experience in a manufacturing environment focused on exotic sheet metal, preferably in aerospace.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in manufacturing engineering, tooling design, and manufacturing process development for metal forming and aerospace sheet metal components; candidates without a degree may require 10–15 years of relevant experience.
  • Experience with sheet metal fabrication methods such as hydroforming, heat treat, brazing, laser cutting, brake forming, welding (TIG and resistance), and NDT processes; in some roles, at least seven (7) years of experience with these methods is required.
  • Proficiency in sheet metal manufacturing methods using metals such as aluminum, nickel alloys, stainless steels, and titanium, with at least seven (7) years of experience in these materials in certain positions.
  • Strong CAD modeling experience, including designing tools and fixtures for sheet metal forming; candidates should have at least seven (7) years of CAD experience and be able to rate their CAD ability at 7/10 or higher.
  • Ability to design tooling for sheet metal forming using CAD, with a minimum of three (3) years of experience with a BS degree or seven (7) years without a degree.
  • Daily, practical command of GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing), demonstrated through consistent use in recent work experience.
  • Experience in process layout and routing creation, typically 3–7 years of hands-on work defining and documenting manufacturing processes.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Project, for documentation, reporting, and project management.
  • Familiarity with ERP systems for managing bills of materials, routings, work orders, and related production data.
  • Understanding and practical use of lean tools such as Six Sigma and value stream mapping (VSM), with at least seven (7) years of experience using these tools in some roles.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific and technical journals, financial reports, legal documents, and customer specifications.
  • Ability to respond professionally to inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community.
  • Ability to effectively present information to immediate supervisors and upper management, both verbally and in writing.
  • Strong mathematical skills, including probability, statistical inference, plane and solid geometry, and trigonometry, applied to manufacturing and process engineering problems.
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, and interpret complex technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form while managing both abstract and concrete variables.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

  • Experience in an aerospace sheet metal manufacturing environment, particularly with exotic metals and complex formed components.
  • Experience with CAD platforms such as SolidWorks, NX, or comparable 3D CAD programs for modeling parts, tools, and fixtures.
  • Experience with multi-axis programming, ideally for laser cutting equipment, though programming experience on other multi-axis machines is also valuable.
  • Background in process engineering, machining, and fixture design to support integrated manufacturing solutions.
  • Experience with heat treat processes and their integration into overall manufacturing process flows.
  • Familiarity with press brake and roll forming operations for aerospace sheet metal components.
  • Experience with Mastercam or similar CAM software for programming machining or cutting operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage project plans and move work forward proactively without waiting for detailed direction at each step.
  • Experience working within AS9100 or similar quality management systems in aerospace or other highly regulated industries.
  • Exposure to continuous improvement initiatives, including 5S and lean manufacturing cell development.
  • Comfort working with clients, vendors, and cross-functional teams to align technical requirements and resolve issues efficiently.

Work Environment

The role is based in an aerospace sheet metal forming contract manufacturing facility operating under AS9100 regulations. The environment centers on the production of complex components made from exotic metals such as aluminum, nickel alloys, stainless steel, and titanium using processes like hydroforming, heat treat, brazing, laser cutting, brake forming, welding (TIG and resistance), NDT, press brake, and roll forming. The Manufacturing Engineer will work closely with production, quality, and inspection teams on the shop floor and in an office setting, using CAD software (such as SolidWorks, NX, or similar), ERP systems, Microsoft Office, and potentially CAM tools like Mastercam. The facility emphasizes lean manufacturing, 5S, and continuous improvement within manufacturing cells, with a strong focus on meeting aerospace quality and regulatory requirements. The organization is growing, adding new programs and customers, and investing in infrastructure and people, offering a dynamic environment with significant opportunities to contribute to new product introductions and long-term program growth.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

Join the Manufacturing Engineering team supporting the Advanced Concepts & Enterprise Engineering business unit, where we provide technical solutions across multiple early-stage development programs. Title: Process Engineer


Location: Providence, RI


Our client, a leading global company specializing in custom solutions for the medical device and pharmaceutical industries, is seeking a Process Engineer for its Providence, RI location. The company designs and manufactures custom components using advanced plastic manufacturing technology and rigorous quality control standards.


Position Overview


The Process Engineer works closely with Operations, Quality, and Design teams to establish and sustain process capability across the company's Americas operations. This role applies engineering principles, statistical methods, and process development expertise to optimize product quality, ensure regulatory compliance, and drive continuous improvement from development through full-scale production.


Responsibilities and Functions:


  • Develop and execute IQ/OQ/PQ validation protocols for thermoforming and sealing processes in compliance with ISO 11607-2 and FDA process validation guidance.
  • Define critical process parameters (CPPs), Proven Acceptable Ranges (PAR), and Normal Operating Ranges (NOR) through structured development studies and DOE.
  • Lead statistical analysis of validation data, including process capability (Cpk), targeting a minimum Cpk of 1.33 for critical parameters.
  • Own the full three-stage validation lifecycle: Process Design, Process Qualification, and Continued Process Verification.
  • Define, optimize, and standardize process parameters including temperature profiles, vacuum/pressure settings, plug assist timing, and cycle times.
  • Lead equipment qualification (IQ/OQ) for supporting equipment.
  • Ensure all processes comply with ISO 13485, ISO 11607-1/2, and FDA 21 CFR Part 820 (QMSR); serve as subject matter expert during internal, customer, and regulatory audits.
  • Use Minitab or equivalent software for DOE, capability studies, SPC, Gage R&R, and process data analysis.
  • Lead PFMEA, CAPA, and root cause investigations using structured methodologies (5-Why, Fishbone, DMAIC).
  • Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Design to align process improvements with business and customer requirements.
  • Train production teams on validated processes, in-process monitoring requirements, and critical quality attributes.
  • Apply Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles to eliminate waste and improve process efficiency.


Qualifications:

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Chemical Engineering, or a related field. Advanced degrees or certifications (Six Sigma, CQE, CQA) are a plus.


Experience:

  • 3–5+ years in process engineering, manufacturing engineering, or operations engineering within a regulated industry; medical device experience strongly preferred.
  • Hands-on experience with process validation (IQ/OQ/PQ).
  • Strong working knowledge of ISO 13485 and FDA 21 CFR Part 820 — must be able to serve as subject matter expert during audits.
  • Demonstrated expertise in DOE and Six Sigma methodology; Black Belt certification preferred.
  • Proficiency with Minitab or equivalent statistical software for capability analysis, SPC, and DOE.
  • Experience with CAPA and structured problem-solving methodologies.
  • Familiarity with plastic manufacturing processes, polymer materials, heat sealing, and packaging equipment.
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to influence across Operations, Quality, and Design.

Job Summary

The Sr Supplier Project Engineer is a key member of the Supplier Engineering group within Insulet's Supply Chain organization. Insulet manages a global supply chain and sources precision components and commodities from around the world for use in its medical devices. In this role, you will partner closely with colleagues and leaders across Quality, Sourcing, R&D and Manufacturing to plan and implement prototype and capital tooling and equipment at our suppliers, drive new product introductions, deliver improvement projects, resolve business-critical technical issues, and lead corrective actions in response to quality concerns across the supply base.

This is a highly visible, cross-functional role for an engineer who is as comfortable on the factory floors, office environments, and supplier locations. Success depends on a solid understanding of product performance with respect to measurement and tolerance, materials and material compatibility, and part and process risk mitigation. The ideal candidate brings project management experience leading cross-functional teams, a strong quality background, and either deep mechanical and automation expertise or strong process and data analysis capability. Experience with suppliers of custom precision components for medical devices, along with Six Sigma or Lean training, is a distinct advantage.

You will influence supplier personnel at every level, from shop floor operators to executive leadership, across Manufacturing, R&D, Quality and Automation, as well as the broader network of partners Insulet does business with.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, plan and implement supplier capital and tooling qualifications from project kick-off through implementation into full production.
  • Own project schedules and assigned budgets, and report status, risks and mitigation plans clearly to stakeholders and leadership.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams across R&D, Quality, Automation and Manufacturing to deliver design-for-manufacturability analysis and support.
  • Author or review supplier validation and qualification protocols, and coordinate their execution, data analysis and final reporting.
  • Lead teams responsible for the procurement, installation and start-up of manufacturing equipment at global suppliers.
  • Evaluate and manage prototype suppliers, place purchase orders and manage part deliveries against program timelines.
  • Investigate supplier quality issues and lead corrective and preventive actions to closure, applying structured part and process risk mitigation.
  • Work effectively in a borderless organization, driving results with teams spanning programs, engineering, purchasing and the supply base.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science in Engineering (Plastics, Mechanical, Biomedical, Manufacturing or Industrial) or a related field.
  • Five to seven years of experience working directly with manufacturing processes such as assembly, automation, molding, stamping, electronics or machining.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple supplier tooling projects from concept to production, including authoring and overseeing IQ, OQ and PQ protocols for component manufacturing processes and secondary operations.
  • Working expertise in PFMEA, control plans and Measurement System Analysis.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to influence without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience inside a direct material supplier as an engineer or project manager.
  • Experience in a regulated industry, ideally medical devices.
  • Six Sigma or Lean process improvement experience or certification.
  • PMI project management certification.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and project management tools such as Smartsheet or Excel.

Travel And Physical Requirements

This position requires travel to supplier sites approximately 10 to 15 percent of the time, concentrated around critical project activities such as prototype builds, tooling trials, equipment installation and qualification runs.

NOTE: This position is eligible for hybrid working arrangements and requires on-site work from an Insulet office.

Additional Information

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.

About Johnson & Johnson MedTech

J&J Robotics was established in 2020 with the integration of Auris Health, Verb Surgical, C-SATS, and Ethicon. It comprises three key med-tech platforms: Surgical Robotics (OTTAVA™), Flexible Robotics (MONARCH®), and Digital Solutions. Join our collaborative, rapidly growing team where you'll create breakthrough medical technologies that unite multiple subject areas to build a connected digital ecosystem that advances medical professionals' skills and improves patient outcomes.

In this role, you will lead manufacturing engineering activities for the precision mechanical and electromechanical systems that enable the OTTAVA™ surgical robotics platform. You will develop, validate, and scale assembly processes, tooling, equipment, and manufacturing controls that translate complex design requirements into reliable production solutions. This is an exciting opportunity to help build the future of surgical robotics.

Fueled by innovation at the intersection of biology and technology, we’re developing the next generation of smarter, less invasive, more personalized treatments.

Are you passionate about improving and expanding the possibilities of surgery? Ready to join a team that’s reimagining how we heal? Our Surgery team will give you the chance to deliver surgical technologies and solutions to surgeons and healthcare professionals around the world. Your contributions will help effectively treat some of the world’s most prevalent conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular disease and cancer. Patients are waiting.

Your unique talents will help patients on their journey to wellness. Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/medtech

Purpose

We are seeking a Senior Manufacturing Mechanical Engineer with exceptional drive and urgency to lead new product introduction, process development, and industrialization activities for our advanced robotic medical device systems.

The successful candidate will bring specialized expertise in surgical robotic arm structures and instrument-drive end mechanisms, leading process design, precision assembly, metrology, and validation for one of the most technically demanding product families in medical robotics.

This role owns the complete manufacturing engineering lifecycle for robotic arm kinematic chains, multi-degree-of-freedom joint assemblies, wrist mechanisms, and instrument drive units, where micron-level assembly precision directly translates to surgical accuracy, patient safety, and clinical outcomes.

The ideal candidate combines deep mechanical intuition with rigorous process engineering discipline, regulatory fluency, and hands-on expertise with the precision measurement and assembly equipment required to build and verify surgical-grade robotic mechanisms at scale.

This role demands someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, takes proactive ownership of complex technical challenges, and can rapidly troubleshoot and resolve manufacturing issues that impact product launches. You’ll be instrumental in bridging design intent and manufacturing reality for next-generation surgical robotics platforms.

Why This Role Matters

You’ll be instrumental in bringing next-generation robotic surgical systems from concept to reality, working on mechanisms that require a high level of precision and reliability. This role offers the opportunity to shape manufacturing strategy early in the product lifecycle, prevent costly delays, and ensure our products can scale while meeting the highest quality standards. If you’re energized by technical challenges, move with urgency, and take pride in getting products across the finish line, this is your opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and own assembly processes for multi-axis robotic arm structures
  • Develop assembly sequence logic that controls the buildup of kinematic error through the arm chain, minimizing cumulative positional error at the tool center point (TCP)
  • Define and validate datum schemes and fixturing strategies that enforce consistent reference frames throughout arm assembly, from individual joint builds through full-arm integration
  • Author assembly processes for complex electromechanical assemblies
  • Define assembly and inspection processes for link structures, including shim and seal installation, bonding, and inspection acceptance criteria
  • Determine joint- and arm-level metrology and instrumentation requirements for assembly reliability and verification
  • Define and implement precision fastening systems, such as smart torque drivers and micro-torque tools, to support reliable assembly and verification
  • Define, source, and implement precision equipment, fixtures, and tools (EFT) for press-fit, bearing, and other mechanical interference assemblies
  • Define, source, and implement precision bonding, potting, lubrication, and dispensing systems
  • Define, source, and implement precision alignment and kinematic assembly fixtures
  • Develop project plans and execute them through implementation
  • Troubleshoot complex mechanical and electromechanical system issues
  • Coach and mentor junior engineers and technicians on manufacturing best practices

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Technical Leadership

  • Establish strong working relationships with R&D, Development Engineering, Operations Process Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Production to design, develop, test, document, and implement processes, tooling, and fixtures
  • Partner with Quality to proactively address and resolve nonconformances before they affect production
  • Identify process requirements, advise operations management, and implement the equipment and fixtures needed for process development and manufacturing
  • Maintain attention to detail while moving with urgency, ensuring that critical actions do not fall through the cracks

Skills

  • Systems-level thinking connecting joint-level assembly precision to full-arm/robotic accuracy
  • Exceptional technical writing capability for regulatory-grade process documentation
  • Strong leadership presence — able to drive alignment across R&D, quality, regulatory, and operations without direct authority
  • Passion for precision and zero-defect manufacturing in a life-critical product environment
  • Deep curiosity about mechanism design and a hands-on instinct for understanding how things are built and how they fail
  • Commitment to building processes that are not just capable today, but robust and scalable as production volumes grow

Qualifications

Education

  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree and/or University degree in mechanical engineering, Mechatronics, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field is required; a Master’s degree is preferred

Required Experience

  • A minimum of four years of manufacturing or assembly engineering experience, including significant experience with surgical robotic arms or comparable precision electromechanical capital equipment
  • Demonstrated expertise in precision joint assembly, including bearing preload, harmonic drives, cable-driven mechanisms, and encoder integration
  • Strong manufacturing engineering background in BOM structures, process documentation (MPI, DHR, and MES), and PFMEA
  • Medical device industry experience preferred; a proven track record in NPI environments is highly valued
  • Electromechanical systems: Extensive troubleshooting capability across mechanical, electrical, and instrumentation domains
  • CAD proficiency: Expert-level skills in CAD design (SolidWorks preferred), ASME Y14.5 GD&T, and 3D tolerance stack-up analysis
  • Strong statistical proficiency in SPC, Cpk, DOE, and Minitab or equivalent tools
  • Quality systems: More than three years of experience at J&J or in an equivalent regulated environment, with demonstrated proficiency in applicable systems, SOPs, and processes

Preferred

  • Experience with surgical robotics platforms
  • Certification: Six Sigma Black Belt
  • Direct experience with surgical robotic platforms
  • Experience with ISO 9283 (manipulator performance evaluation) and robotic arm kinematic calibration
  • Familiarity with EtherCAT, CAN bus, or real-time motion control communication architectures
  • Experience with micro-assembly processes and magnification-assisted assembly techniques
  • Knowledge of carbon fiber composite structural assembly and inspection
  • Experience with MES systems and PLM tools in regulated industries

Other

  • May require up to 10% domestic and/or international travel to other locations and sites

Manufacturing Engineer

Passion:

jobTitle: Senior Manufacturing Process Development Engineer - Medical
jobDescription:
About Us

Founded in 2015 to develop the world’s first industrially scalable laser metal additive manufacturing solution, VulcanForms is reshaping how the world manufactures critical products. We build and operate advanced digital infrastructure that enables innovation, accelerates growth, and supports sustainability across aerospace, defense, medical, and other essential industries. Through our vertically integrated capabilities, including scalable additive manufacturing and precision machining, we deliver true end-to-end production at scale by combining cutting-edge technology with a foundation of proven industrial craftsmanship. Our team brings deep expertise in manufacturing, materials science, software, automation, and operations, united by a shared commitment to quality, curiosity, and accountability. We foster an inclusive culture where people take ownership, solve meaningful problems, and continuously learn, because we believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes.

Job Purpose

The Senior Manufacturing Process Development Engineer will establish and optimize reliable processes, working cross-functionally to deliver safe, efficient processes that meet quality, cost, capacity, and customer requirements within our Medical business unit. This role will work cross-functionally on NPI teams to support process development and help successfully sample and launch new products. This role will also be responsible for taking new products from post-print to finished product by developing and scaling robust post-processing operations. They will provide technical leadership for the Production Team, define process requirements, coordinate with suppliers, and implement tooling and equipment solutions for post-processing printed parts and components.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define and support post-processing steps (e.g., machining, blasting, deburring, cleaning, heat treating) for new product; turn product designs and requirements into robust, scalable manufacturing processes.
  • Oversee the implementation of manufacturing processes by collaborating with in-house technicians and external suppliers. Coordinate machine setup and process validation while maintaining technical ownership.
  • Define functional requirements for tooling, fixturing, and post-processing equipment, including identifying opportunities for automation or capital investment to improve productivity. Partner with suppliers to deliver reliable solutions, and lead their implementation, testing, and validation.
  • Write and maintain detailed work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and process documentation to ensure repeatable and high-quality production.
  • Lead Installation Qualifications (IQ) for manufacturing equipment and support QC and Quality Engineering in Operational and Performance Qualifications (OQ/PQ). Help ensure all processes meet quality and regulatory requirements.

About The Role


The Sr. Process Development Engineer will be responsible to bridge early-stage device development and commercial-grade manufacturing. This individual will take first-in-human catheter devices and refine them into robust, manufacturable products ready for commercial launch. The ideal candidate will bring deep catheter engineering expertise, a manufacturing mindset, and a proven track record of successful medical device design transfer.


To Make An Impact, You Will


  • Lead process development activities to transition early-stage catheter devices from first-in-human configurations to commercially viable, scalable products.
  • Perform DFM/DFA analyses and tolerance stack-up studies (worst-case and statistical) to eliminate producibility risks, define critical dimensions, and establish component acceptance criteria.
  • Develop and maintain detailed component specifications, drawing requirements, and incoming inspection criteria, including AQL sampling plans, in alignment with device performance requirements and supplier capabilities.
  • Characterize and optimize catheter manufacturing processes including extrusion, braiding, tip forming, thermal bonding, adhesive joining, and laser cutting to achieve robust, repeatable outcomes.
  • Develop and optimize electrical assembly processes for catheter-integrated components, including fine-gauge wire termination, surface mount component placement, and high- and low-voltage cable assembly fabrication in compliance with applicable industry workmanship standards.
  • Partner with Manufacturing Engineering on process validation (IQ, OQ, PQ) and process FMEAs; contribute to protocols, risk documentation, and control definitions to ensure regulatory compliance.
  • Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering to establish SPC methods, capability studies (Cp, Cpk), yield targets, and build monitoring frameworks that support production stability and COGS objectives.
  • Develop inspection gauges and conduct MSA/gauge R&R studies to validate measurement system capability.
  • Evaluate and qualify raw materials, adhesives, and components; assess material compatibility, processability, and biocompatibility implications.
  • Initiate and manage engineering change orders (ECOs) to implement process improvements while maintaining design history file integrity.
  • Ensure components and processes under development are compatible with sterilization methods (EO, gamma, e-beam) and packaging requirements in collaboration with quality and regulatory teams.
  • Apply lean manufacturing principles to reduce waste and improve cycle times in preparation for commercial scale-up.
  • Partner with suppliers and contract manufacturers to evaluate process capabilities, establish manufacturing requirements, and drive continuous improvement.
  • Create and maintain manufacturing work instructions, assembly procedures, and process travelers to support design transfer and production readiness.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with R&D, quality, regulatory, and manufacturing teams to align process activities with design controls and program timelines.
  • Mentor junior engineers and technicians on process-related problem solving and root cause analysis.


To Excel, You Will Bring


  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Materials Science, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.
  • Minimum 5 years of medical device process development or manufacturing engineering experience, with at least 3 years focused on catheter-based devices, including demonstrated experience taking a device from early-stage development to commercial manufacturing.
  • Hands-on experience with catheter manufacturing processes including extrusion, braiding, thermal bonding, tip forming, adhesive assembly, and laser processing.
  • Proficiency in tolerance stack-up analysis (worst-case and statistical) and working knowledge of statistical methods (Cp/Cpk, SPC, gauge R&R); DOE experience a plus.
  • Experience supporting process validation (IQ, OQ, PQ) in a regulated medical device environment.
  • Familiarity with FDA QSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, and ISO 14971 risk management requirements.
  • Experience developing component specifications and working with suppliers to establish and verify manufacturing capabilities.
  • Proficient in CAD tools (SolidWorks preferred) and GD&T per ASME Y14.5; familiarity with statistical software (Minitab or equivalent) preferred.
  • Working knowledge of catheter materials including thermoplastic polymers (PEBAX, nylon, polyurethane, PTFE), metallic components (nitinol, stainless steel, platinum-iridium), and adhesive systems.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; experience with root cause analysis tools including FMEA, fishbone diagrams, 8D, and 5 Whys.
  • Cleanroom experience preferred (ISO Class 7 or 8); strong project management skills with ability to manage multiple concurrent programs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.
  • Ability to work conscientiously and with minimal direction, using good judgement and taking initiative to accomplish assigned tasks.
  • Ability to work as a team member, multi-task, and adapt to the changing priorities of a dynamic, fast-growing company.
  • Occasional travel may be required up to 15% of the time, primarily for supplier qualification, contract manufacturing, and design transfer activities.
  • Ability to lift 10-15 pounds.

Title: Staff Manufacturing Engineer

Company Summary: Join a team that's redefining what's possible in cardiovascular treatment. At Jupiter Endovascular, we're revolutionizing catheter-based therapies by bringing the precision and control of surgery to minimally invasive procedures. For decades, catheters have remained largely unchanged—rigid, unstable, and difficult to maneuver through the body's winding anatomy. We've developed a transforming fixation technology that navigates flexibly through the vascular system, then locks into place to deliver treatment with surgical-like stability and control.

Our device solves one of the longest-standing challenges in endovascular procedures, empowering physicians and improving outcomes for millions of patients living with cardiovascular disease. We're entering an exciting new phase—scaling up production, expanding our team, and preparing for commercial launch.

Founded and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, Jupiter Endovascular is led by a proven team of medical device entrepreneurs and backed by top-tier investors across venture capital, private equity, and strategic partners. We've built a fast-paced, collaborative culture grounded in innovation, teamwork, and purpose. Every role at Jupiter directly contributes to our mission: saving lives by advancing the future of endovascular therapy.

Position Overview: The Staff Manufacturing Engineer will be a core team member of our growing manufacturing/process development team leading early development of novel manufacturing processes and paving the way for our scale up to commercial launch. The ideal candidate would act with passion and intensity in a medical device start-up that is fast-paced and collaborative and would display the ability to perform the requirements outlined below. You will design fixturing and tooling in SolidWorks, help source and commission production equipment including robotics and automation cells, provide day-to-day engineering support on the floor, and use process data to find and fix the steps that limit quality or throughput. You will work alongside experienced manufacturing engineers who will hand you real projects early rather than have you shadow theirs, and you will learn how manufacturing works inside a regulated quality system as you go.

  • Design semi-automated, automated, and manual fixturing and tooling for manufacturing operations, including both digital and physical tools.

  • Train production personnel on new and revised processes, and support continuous improvement and quality projects.

  • An internship or co-op in medical device or another regulated manufacturing environment is a plus.

Job Summary

Johnson & Johnson MedTech is seeking a Senior Manufacturing Engineer to support digital and manufacturing operations in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida.

This role supports robotics, process development, tool design, manufacturing flow, continuous improvement, and engineering support of production. The Senior Manufacturing Engineer provides direction and technical support for equipment design and development, testing of materials, preparation of specifications and operator instructions, process studies, investigations, root cause analysis, problem solving, report and presentation preparation, project management, statistical analysis, presentation of data, and technical writing. This role also supports the implementation of new technologies, process development, evaluation of process quality, cost, capacity, and capability alternatives, while ensuring manufacturing areas meet quality standards, compliant documentation requirements, capacity, product availability, and cost objectives.


Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as a fully competent engineer in conventional aspects of the assigned subject matter, functional area, and responsibilities.
  • Participate in multi-site projects and lead complex engineering projects, either technically or with an extensive cross-functional team.
  • Develop and execute project plans and schedules, meet project goals and objectives, track costs, prepare status reports, conduct meetings, and document and communicate progress to management.
  • Lead and participate in investigations, develop plans, and execute tasks to solve process problems, including nonconformances, complaint investigations, audit observations, and corrective and preventive actions.
  • Perform analysis and communicate associated trends.
  • Provide day-to-day support and direction to Production, including turning, milling, drilling, EDM, finishing, packaging, and other manufacturing activities as required.
  • Develop process validation strategy and lead validation execution, including engineering studies, process validation protocols, and summary reports.
  • Write and execute Installation Qualification, Operational Qualification, Performance Qualification, Computer Software Validation, and Test Method Validation documentation.
  • Identify, lead, and implement process improvements for existing manufacturing processes using appropriate engineering principles and standard strategies, including Lean and Six Sigma principles.
  • Perform gage design, measurement system analysis, and gage implementation as required.
  • Use measuring instruments such as micrometers, calipers, comparators, tensile testers, coordinate measurement systems, and other tools to support engineering testing.
  • Lead the design and development of fixtures and tools and collaborate effectively with tool designers to express and implement ideas.
  • Lead new equipment acquisition efforts, including user requirement specifications, machine selection, installation, validation, employee training, and related equipment responsibilities.
  • Develop and implement manufacturing and inspection procedures.
  • Participate in and lead cross-functional teams, which may include Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Quality Assurance, Finance, Product Development, and personnel from other sites.
  • Act as a liaison to vendors regarding contracted products, tools, fixtures, and manufacturing support.
  • Identify and implement improvements to engineering business processes, including configuration management, ERP management, maintenance tracking, and related systems.
  • Perform other related duties as required.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor of Science degree from an accredited institution in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related degree is required.

Required Experience & Skills

  • 2-4 years of experience in manufacturing and/or engineering is required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing principles, practices, and procedures.
  • Experience supporting process development, manufacturing flow, tooling, fixtures, equipment, and production engineering activities.
  • Ability to lead investigations, perform root cause analysis, and solve complex process problems.
  • Ability to deliver clear oral and written communications around process improvement projects.
  • Strong organizational, project management, troubleshooting, analytical, interpersonal, and computer skills, including Microsoft Office, Minitab, and Visio.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master of Science degree from an accredited institution in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related degree is preferred.
  • Previous experience working in a regulated industry, such as medical device, is preferred.
  • Experience in the medical device industry or medical field is preferred.
  • Familiarity with FDA, GMP, and ISO requirements is preferred.
  • Six Sigma or Lean Sigma certification or 4 years of related experience is preferred.
  • Six Sigma Black Belt and Lean certifications are preferred.

  • The candidate will also work to develop skills necessary to be able to connect changes in component geometry to its functional performance via correlation and emulation of aerodynamic & structural physics responses.
  • You will be a leader in root cause investigations addressing challenges with low First Pass Yield (FPY), high Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and low throughput.
  • The selected candidate will utilize their Data Science and Statistical expertise in gathering & analyzing large datasets, deploy inductive & deductive investigative tools, and recommend solutions.
  • As a Manufacturing Engineer, the candidate’s skills in operations optimization and data analytics will also be used to support other functions such as Continuous Improvement, Waste Reduction (Lean), and general business performance.
  • To execute the desired process improvement, the candidate will be responsible for project planning, collaborating with various engineering disciplines, and influencing management to implement the desired solutions.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Develop and Monitor Multivariate Process Controls using both traditional SPC rules and custom methods.
  • Lead root cause investigations and work with process owners to execute solution implementation.
  • Relate Key Process Inputs to Process Outputs with tools like PFMEAs or Characteristics Matrices.
  • Identify relationships between Part Geometry and Part Performance with Designed Experiments (DOE) and statistical modeling.
  • Perform ad-hoc data analysis requests to support business improvement objectives.
  • Assemble, Lead and Present Monthly MCAB (Manufacturing Corrective action Board) Meetings
  • Ensure Business Maintains Compliance to the requirements of deviations, MSPC and FA.  


Qualifications You Must Have:

  • 2+ Years of related experience

  • Experience with databases/data warehouses and constructing queries
  • Strong communication and influencing skills

  • Six Sigma Green Belt or Red-X Apprentice experience

  • Database/data warehouse and query experience with Databricks, SQL, and Python preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead root cause investigations, propose corrective actions & technical solutions, and execute on the implementation of those actions.

Mission

The Manufacturing Engineer – Optical Systems & Sustaining Engineering serves as a key technical resource for optical and laser-based manufacturing technologies. This role supports both New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining engineering activities, contributing to the development, deployment, and continual improvement of optical systems, laser illumination

systems, and precision opto-mechanical assemblies.

The engineer will provide technical leadership in manufacturing readiness, process development, production support, troubleshooting, and workforce training while serving as a mentor and consultant to technicians and manufacturing personnel.

Position Summary

As a member of the Manufacturing Engineering team, you will be responsible for leading the development, optimization, and sustaining manufacturing processes for optical products and systems. The successful candidate will possess strong technical knowledge in one of the following: optics, lasers, or optical assemblies. A key element is an emphasis on precision

manufacturing while demonstrating the ability to rapidly learn new technologies and effectively lead the transition into

production.

This role supports multiple active product development programs and existing production lines, ensuring successful product launches, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the manufacturing value stream.

All members of the Manufacturing Engineering team are expected to embody the company's values of Team, Trust, and Excellence.

Key Responsibilities

New Product Introduction & Manufacturing Readiness

• Lead the transition of new optical and laser-based products into manufacturing.

• Implement robust manufacturing processes, work instructions, test methods, and training.

• Collaborate with R&D teams during product development to ensure manufacturability and production scalability.

• Support stage-gate development activities and manufacturing readiness reviews.

• Support qualification & validate manufacturing process and test stations prior to release.

Optical Systems Engineering

• Align and optimize optical tabletop systems and production optical assemblies.

• Support optical system integration, metrology, testing, and performance verification.

• Apply knowledge of optical principles, system tolerancing, and opto-mechanical integration.

• Support laser illumination systems, optical alignment techniques, and detector-based measurements.

• Develop fixtures, tooling, and automation to improve manufacturing efficiency and quality.

Sustaining Engineering

• Support existing products through continuous improvement, cost reduction, quality improvement, and obsolescence mitigation initiatives.

• Investigate and resolve manufacturing, supplier, and/or quality issues.

• Drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) and root cause analysis activities.

• Partner with Operations and Quality teams to improve production performance and customer satisfaction.

• Maintain technical documentation including work instructions, process specifications, and manufacturing standards.

Production Support & Continuous Improvement

• Provide technical support for production ramp activities and manufacturing operations.

• Mentor technicians and production personnel in troubleshooting, process execution, and continuous improvement.

• Identify and implement productivity improvements through Lean Manufacturing.

• Improve production throughput, yield, labor efficiency, and operational performance.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Optics, Optical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Minimum 5 years of manufacturing engineering experience maintaining existing products and scaling up production throughput.

• Experience leading the transfer of technology from development into manufacturing.

• Experience developing manufacturing processes, documentation, and training programs.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to lead projects and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in one or more of the following areas:

• Optical assembly, alignment, and metrology

• Precision lens manufacturing and optical system production

• Laser illumination systems

• Opto-mechanical assemblies

• Optical tabletop setup and alignment

• Optical testing, detectors, and data acquisition systems

• New Product Introduction with production ramp-up and manufacturing readiness activities.

• Sustaining engineering in a production environment

Success Metrics

Performance in this position will be measured through:

• Successful on-time project execution

• Improved manufacturing readiness and production launch success

• Reduced dependency on Manufacturing Engineering and R&D after production handoff

• Effective resolution of production, supplier, and customer quality issues

• Successful scaling of manufacturing operations to support growth programs

• Development of robust manufacturing processes and technical capability within the organization

Strategic Impact

This position will directly support the organization's growth strategy by:

• Expanding manufacturing engineering capacity to support multiple development programs.

• Providing critical expertise in optics, lens manufacturing, and laser-based systems.

• Reducing single-point-of-failure risks within key technical disciplines.

• Improving manufacturing readiness and production launch performance.

• Supporting current products while enabling successful NPI execution.

• Enhancing responsiveness to customer, quality, and obsolescence-related challenges.

• Driving operational scalability as additional programs move into production.

• Enabling dedicated focus on productivity, automation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys leading technical teams, solving complex technical challenges, working with advanced optical technologies, and building scalable manufacturing solutions that directly impact product success and organizational growth.

Company Profile

With over 80 years of innovation, JCB is the world’s largest privately owned manufacturer of construction and agricultural equipment. Operating 23 manufacturing facilities across four continents—including the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and Brazil—JCB produces a diverse portfolio of more than 300 products. These include telescopic handlers, backhoe loaders, excavators, wheel loaders, compact excavators, skid steer loaders, compact track loaders, access aerial work platforms, rough terrain forklifts, and tractors.

 

At the heart of JCB’s success are its people. As a family-owned business, we are accountable to our customers—not shareholders—which gives us the flexibility to focus on long-term innovation and delivering real value. This independence allows us to continuously develop advanced technologies and integrate them into equipment designed to perform in the toughest environments while maximizing customer productivity.

 

At JCB, we stand behind our products—and our name—with pride and commitment to quality.

This role is part of the Lunar Permanence business unit, which develops Blue Origin’s Blue Moon landers and related products. To further Blue Origin's mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth, we are building sustainable infrastructure for our transport of crew and cargo from Earth to the lunar surface.

This individual will use their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to join our team and positively impact safe human spaceflight. You will work directly with NASA and our National Team Partners as part of the Human Landing System (HLS) Sustaining Lunar Development (SLD) program. You will play a key role in developing the Lunar Permanence system that will return humans to the Moon and extend human presence permanently beyond the bounds of Earth.

This opportunity will report to the Docking Mechanisms Subsystem inside of the Lunar Permanence business unit.  As part of a growing, hardworking, and curious team of design engineers, you’ll be deployed to programs that shape the future of Blue Origin. Your skill in the design and analysis of spacecraft mechanisms as well as your ability to deliver safe, reliable, ready to install hardware that meets requirements, while doing so within the allocated cost and schedule requirements, will lead to a rewarding career with Blue Origin. 

We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To: 

  • Design and develop safety critical mechanical components and systems for pressurized docking mechanisms.  

  • Participate in the entire design cycle of flight hardware, including conceptual and detailed design, trade studies, structural analysis, development testing, and qualification. Generate component drawings, assembly drawings, and interface control documents with application of GD&T per ASME Y14.5. 

  • Create documentation for assembly and testing of development and flight hardware. Participate in subsystem level testing including planning, execution, data reduction and analysis. Develop component specifications and manage suppliers. 

  • Leverage experience and engineering judgment to quickly design and produce non-flight, proof of concept hardware for fast-moving research and development projects 

  • Participate in a small, agile team to create and adapt to frequently shifting priorities 

Minimum Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering 

  • 5+ years of experience designing aerospace or equivalent type mechanical system elements within aircraft, spacecraft, or launch vehicles 

  • Strong mechanical design, integration, and mechanism analysis skills using 3D modeling and simulation tools (CREO preferred). 

  • Knowledge of manufacturing, assembly, integration, and qualification testing 

  • Proficient in technical writing, communicating sophisticated ideas clearly and concisely 

  • Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with spacecraft docking systems design, analysis, test, qualification, and production

  • Familiarity with docking system standards, such as the International Docking System Standard (IDSS) and Gateway Docking System Standard (GDSS).

  • Knowledge of aerospace mechanisms design practices & standards including applicable NASA specifications such as NASA-STD-5017.

  • Experience with GD&T analysis (ASME Y14.5) and performing tolerance stacks 

  • Fluency in mechanisms avionics interfaces and control logic

  • Background including mechanical finite element analysis statics and dynamics

  • Experience with thermal design of spacecraft structures & mechanisms

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

We are looking for you to join our team as a Engineer Manufacturing / Principal Engineer Manufacturing based out of Sunnyvale, CA.

You will support the manufacturing and testing of marine propulsion and power generations systems working on various manufacturing processes for high value gearing and steam turbine assemblies, machined components, and welded fabrications.

What You'll get to Do:

  • Develop new processes, improve existing manufacturing processes, and develop the required tooling and fixtures with an excellent team of experienced assembly mechanics, machinists, welders and engineers.

  • Adapts machine or equipment design to factory and production conditions.

  • Evaluate existing manufacturing processes and systems to reduce cost, improve sustainability and develop best practices within the manufacturing environment.

  • Develop efficient process flows and sequences of operations, optimized production area layouts, manage bills of materials, and create detailed work instructions, process procedures and tooling requirements with emphasis on safety, foreign object elimination and equipment/system maintenance.

  • Support continuous improvement initiatives and implementation of new capital equipment for establishing expanded production processes.

  • Select roles will also support final acceptance testing of product and provide technical support to test facility operation as necessary.

  • The ability to support multiple production shifts is required (first, second, third shifts, and weekends) based on the assignment and current and future production schedules.

This position may be filled at the Machining Manufacturing Engineer or Principal Machining Manufacturing Engineer level based on experience.

Basic Qualifications for the Machining Manufacturing Engineer:

  • Bachelor's degree with a minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience; OR a master's degree with 1 or more years of relevant work experience.

  • Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings.

  • Experience with machining and machine shops.

  • Experience with mechanical assembly processes, welding and machining.

  • Experience in technical writing.

  • Ability to obtain a US Government Secret Clearance.

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES/COMPETENCIES

 

  • Problem Solving: Handle day-to-day problems with processes, product, equipment and documentation.  Investigate and complete assigned Corrective Action Requests, working with assigned Business Unit team to systematically identify and address root cause. Assist and coordinate with maintenance and facility engineering for process and equipment troubleshooting to support production goals and reduce downtime.

  • Experience with metal-joining processes (Tig, resistance welding, brazing) preferred

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 JOB PURPOSE: The Manufacturing Engineer I supports manufacturing operations by applying engineering principles within a designated production area and assisting with customer-driven projects.   • Collaborate effectively with Production, Quality, Project Engineering, and Supply Chain teams to support manufacturing goals and customer requirements.
  • Apply independent judgment and engineering fundamentals to evaluate manufacturing processes and recommend improvements under the guidance of senior engineering staff.

  • Experience, Competencies and Education
  • Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering field required.

Ability to read, analyze and interpret technical documents, work instructions, specifications, and procedures relevant to the role.  

  • Mathematical Skills

Ability to perform basic mathematical equations relevant to manufacturing and engineering tasks. 

  • Reasoning Ability

Ability to manage a variety of job assignments, apply logical reasoning, and solve routine manufacturing-related problems with guidance as needed.

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft Outlook
  • Basic CAD software
  • General internet and computer use

  • Previous experience in a manufacturing or production environment preferred.

  • Exposure to Lean Manufacturing principles or Six Sigma methodologies.
  • Experience with ERP systems or basic manufacturing- related data entry.

ACCOUNTABILITIES AND MEASURES

  • Timely and accurate completion of assigned engineering tasks and project deliverables.
  • Adherence to the Company Quality Policy and ISO procedural requirements.
  • Compliance with safety policies, housekeeping standards, and good manufacturing practices.
  • Ability to work independently, follow established work rules, remain flexible, and perform a variety of engineering support tasks as required.

Who we are

About Bridge

We're creating an entirely new payments platform, built with stablecoins, to simplify global money movement. Bridge enables faster, cheaper payments and borderless access to dollars via stablecoins. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders faster and cheaper vs. SWIFT and other fiat-only rails. Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We believe many trillions of dollars will move and settle through stablecoin payment rails. Bridge is pulling this future forward.

We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that allows for the improvement of global money movement.

About The Team

Join our Issuance Product team to shape the future of financial access and infrastructure. We're not just improving global payments, we're reinventing them with modern rails that allow for fast, cheap transactions at any size. You will build a platform that powers issuing compliant stablecoins in US/EU and beyond. We work with some of the largest fintechs, crypto companies, blockchains and more. This is your chance to lead meaningful innovation from day one, redefining the way businesses and people exchange value globally.

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

  • Build a world class issuance platform that has the scale to power billions of dollars of transactions and issued stablecoins. Product areas include liquidity delivery, reserves management, mint/burn infrastructure, rewards, on-chain/crypto smart contracts, and launching custom stablecoins.
  • Drive product features from ideation to launch, collaborating with designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners such as legal and compliance.
  • Develop a deep understanding of our users’ needs, operational landscape, and competitive environment across international markets.
  • Own outcomes end-to-end, using data, feedback, and rapid iteration to refine your approach.
  • Make tough prioritization calls, balancing user needs, technical feasibility, and business impact.
  • Drive high-traffic features at scale, ensuring security, speed, and reliability for millions of users.


Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

  • Empathy for users: You’re passionate about uncovering and solving pain points.

As the leading end-to-end investment platform for single-family rental homes (SFR), our mission is to reinvent the rental housing ecosystem for the benefit of all. About the Role

The Senior Product Manager, Leasing is the dedicated product leader for Leasing on the Leasing & Resident Experience team. This is a hands-on, high-ownership position over a revenue-carrying surface for someone who thrives at the intersection of Product, Operations, and Growth. You will own the leasing roadmap end to end, deliver the products that help our teams lease more homes faster, and shape new leasing offerings for the landlords who manage on their own.

This role is built for an operator-minded product manager with a bias toward action, a focus on driving outcomes, strong written communication, and a genuine curiosity about how homes actually get leased. If you look at a leasing pipeline and your first instinct is to find the stage where prospects quietly stall, then fix the system so it stops happening, this is your job.

What You'll Own

Product Strategy and Roadmap

  • Own the leasing product roadmap across our retail, institutional, and build-to-rent portfolios, balancing platform commitments against growth opportunities
  • Lead initiatives from discovery through execution, partnering with Engineering and Design on scoping, rollout planning, and post-launch impact analysis
  • Keep priorities, sizing, and sequencing legible so leadership, engineering, and operations are all reading from the same plan

Leasing Funnel Performance

  • Build the visibility and workflow layer for the leasing funnel so handoffs, service levels, and automation status are clear and the team sees what needs attention without digging
  • Partner with leasing operations to remove bottlenecks and help the team absorb more volume without proportionally adding headcount
  • Understand how AI is working within the leasing funnel, from screening to scheduling to prospect communication, well enough to push automation where it helps and catch quality issues before customers do

New Leasing Offerings

  • Shape and validate new leasing products and services for self-managing landlords, from customer discovery through pricing and business modeling
  • Partner with Growth and go-to-market teams to take new offerings from thesis to launch

Customer Research and Insight

  • Talk directly to the people who live in the funnel, including owners, prospects, leasing agents, and screeners, and synthesize what you hear into decisions the team can act on
  • Build and maintain the feedback loops that keep operational signals flowing into product decisions in real time, not after the damage is done

Cross-functional Operations

  • Serve as the product counterpart to Engineering and Design and the point of contact for cross-team dependencies across sales, operations, and account management
  • Support prioritization decisions by balancing strategic goals and operational capacity

Data and Metrics

  • Own leasing funnel metrics end to end, including conversion, speed to lease, service-level adherence, and vacancy
  • Develop and track KPIs that surface risks and opportunities early, and identify root causes when results deviate from expectations

What We're Looking For

  • 5 or more years of product management experience, including ownership of a revenue-carrying product surface at a software company
  • Proptech, real estate, or marketplace background strongly preferred; leasing or property management context is a strong plus. You should know, or be hungry to learn, how a home actually gets leased
  • Grit. You've shipped through ambiguity and constraint, and you can tell us how
  • Strong roadmap and stakeholder management. You can hold deadline-bound platform work and growth bets in the same quarter and keep both moving
  • Comfort in an operator-heavy business; your best discovery starts by shadowing the people doing the work today
  • AI fluency. You use AI tools every day and have opinions about where agents belong in a workflow. You don't need to write code, but you should have put AI into a product, not just into your own productivity
  • Comfort working with data; you can define funnel metrics, read a dashboard, and root-cause a number that moved the wrong way

The Role

General Motors pioneers the innovations that move and connect people to what matters. We see a world with zero crashes, zero emissions, and zero congestion. The Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Product Management organization is responsible for defining and delivering GM’s autonomous driving roadmap—from near‑term customer value to long‑term eyes‑off autonomy at scale.   • Ability to navigate ambiguity and drive projects forward, even without a clear path.

At CancerIQ, our technology is expanding access to precision cancer prevention, early detection and treatment to more patient populations.
